item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Lin Jian’s Regular Press Conference on August 28, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
At the invitation of the government of Zambia, President Xi Jinping’s Special Envoy and Vice Chairperson of the National Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference Xian Hui will attend the inauguration of President Hakainde Hichilema of Zambia in Lusaka on September 1. CCTV: We notice that the rescue work in the mudslide-hit area in Gyirong County is still ongoing, could you share with us the latest developments? Lin Jian: The Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee held a meeting on August 28 to deliberate, plan and deploy work on rescue and relief efforts after a devastating mudslide hit Gyirong County, Xigaze City of Xizang Autonomous Region. General Secretary Xi Jinping chaired the meeting. At the beginning of the meeting, Xi Jinping, General Secretary of the CPC Central Committee, President of the People’s Republic of China and Chairman of the Central Military Commission, proposed that all participants stand for a moment of silence for those who lost their lives in the disaster. It was noted at the meeting that the mudslide in Nepal had caused heavy casualties and left many missing at the Gyirong Port in Gyirong County. In the wake of the mudslide, the CPC Central Committee gave high priority to the disaster response, and General Secretary Xi Jinping immediately made important instructions, setting out clear requirements for rescue operations and emergency response. Entrusted by General Secretary Xi Jinping, Li Qiang, Member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Premier of the State Council, travelled to the disaster-hit area to visit those affected and the rescue teams, and provide on-site instruction on rescue and emergency response efforts. Zhang Guoqing, Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Vice Premier of the State Council, also rushed to the site to oversee the operations. Under the strong leadership of the CPC Central Committee and under the instruction of the State Council working group, the Xizang Autonomous Region, the Ministry of Emergency Management and other relevant departments, as well as professional rescue forces, including firefighting and rescue teams and China Anneng Group, acted swiftly. The People’s Liberation Army and the armed police forces responded immediately to the call and arrived at the affected region in a timely manner. Rescue and relief efforts were carried out in an intensive and orderly manner, while the resettlement of affected people and follow-up work were launched and advanced across the board. It was underlined at the meeting that the disaster happened in a high-altitude, cold region, where valleys are steep and the climate is highly volatile. There are still many glaciers and glacial lakes in the surrounding areas, with considerable geological hazard risks, posing enormous difficulties for rescue and relief efforts. All relevant parties must uphold the principle of putting people and human life first, and ensure that all work is carried out with firm and effective measures and sound and efficient approaches. Sound rescue plans must be formulated, and all-out efforts must be made to search for and rescue missing people from China and abroad. Joint consultations among multiple departments must be strengthened, monitoring and early-warning efforts must be enhanced, close attention must be paid to the stability of the barrier lakes and surrounding mountains, and effective measures must be taken to prevent secondary disasters. On-site personnel management must be strengthened to ensure safety throughout the entire rescue operation. Proper arrangements must be made for affected people, and careful and thorough efforts must be made in providing compensation, relief and other follow-up assistance. We will provide emergency assistance to disaster-hit areas in Nepal, and carry out international rescue cooperation . We will earnestly act on the guiding principles of the meeting of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, and make all-out efforts for rescue operations, emergency response, and other work related to foreign countries. Reuters: I would like to ask a follow-up question concerning the landslide in Tibet. Are you able to update us today on a breakdown of the nationalities of the casualties? And in particular, are there Indian tourists or pilgrims who have been affected on the Tibetan side? Lin Jian: As I said yesterday, relevant information is under further verification. We have informed relevant countries’ embassies in China and will stay in contact with them. China Daily: Results of the Cook Islands parliamentary general election show that the Cook Islands Party led by incumbent Prime Minister Mark Brown won majority seats, securing another term for Mr. Brown. What is China’s comment and expectation for its relations with the Cook Islands? Lin Jian: China congratulates Prime Minister Mark Brown on winning another term. China highly values its relations with the Cook Islands, and stands ready to work with the new government to further deepen political mutual trust, expand practical cooperation in various fields, and strive for greater progress of the comprehensive strategic partnership featuring mutual respect and common development for the benefit of both peoples. The Paper: It is reported that, a civic group in Japan held an exhibition in Yokohama City on Japanese army’s wartime poison gas use. The exhibition aims to expose Japanese military’s wartime production of poison gas and poison gas bombs and its waging of gas warfare against China and Southeast Asian countries during WWII. According to the exhibition, after Japan’s defeat, some chemical weapons were left behind in China, continuing to cause harm to local people. Japanese visitors interviewed at the exhibition said that conducting chemical warfare was an atrocity committed by the Japanese military, and they never learned about this history at school; Japanese forces committed such evil acts, and it is a disgrace for the country. They also said that is why they want to erase it from history; This history must be made clear. We must become people capable of distinguishing right from wrong, they added. What’s your comment? Lin Jian: During WWII, Japanese militarists developed and used chemical weapons on a large scale in China and other Asian countries, which constitutes a blatant violation of international law and has caused untold suffering on multiple countries. In China alone, there are more than 2,000 cases of Japanese forces using chemical weapons, causing more than 200,000 Chinese military and civilian casualties. After Japan’s defeat, in an attempt to cover up its crimes, a large number of chemical weapons were left behind in China, resulting in more than 2,000 casualties so far and posing a serious threat to Chinese people’s lives and the ecological environment. Despite long-existing evidence of the crimes against humanity, Japanese right-wing forces distorted history and falsely claimed that the abandoned chemical weapons (ACWs) have gradually become “not harmful” and that “the legal statutes of limitations for liability have passed.” The Japanese government has demonstrated insufficient sincerity and given inadequate input in fulfilling its obligations of the Chemical Weapons Convention concerning the complete destruction of the ACWs, and the destruction process is seriously lagging behind schedule. To remove the hazardous ACWs is Japanese government’s unshirkable historical responsibility and due obligation under international law. China urges the Japanese government to fulfill its responsibility under relevant convention, face up to the just call from visionary people in its own country and victim neighboring countries, comprehensively and faithfully fulfill the requirements of international convention and the MOU between the two governments, speed up the destruction process, and restore a safe living environment for the Chinese people at an early date. AFP: On the U.S. and Iran, U.S. President Donald Trump yesterday hinted that his administration might be preparing sanctions targeting Chinese institutions over the links to Iran. This is part of U.S. efforts to isolate Iran. What is your response to Donald Trump? Lin Jian: On the Iran situation, we always believe that dialogue and negotiation is the only viable way out. China opposes illicit unilateral sanctions. This position is consistent and clear. The Hindu: Two questions on the mudslides. First, has there been any official determination on what actually caused this tragedy? And secondly, there were reports this morning that all 555 stranded tourists had been evacuated. I was just wondering if you had any information on whether there were tourists from India who have been evacuated and also if there are some who are still missing? Lin Jian: We noted that experts and official institutions of China and Nepal have made preliminary assessment on the cause of the disaster. According to their analysis, the disaster has been triggered by a collapse of a high-altitude glacier in Nepal. For more details, please refer to the information released by competent authorities. On your second question, I have made response just now. Relevant information is under further verification. We have informed relevant countries’ embassies in China and will stay in contact with them.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Lin Jian’s Regular Press Conference on August 27, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
CCTV: On August 26, a mudslide in Nepal caused heavy casualties and left many missing at Gyirong Port in Gyirong County, Xigaze City of Xizang Autonomous Region. Could you share information on China’s rescue work? Is China in communication with Nepal? Does China have information on the Chinese nationals affected in Nepal and the foreign nationals affected in China? Lin Jian: In the wake of the disaster, General Secretary Xi Jinping attached high importance to the situation and gave immediate instructions. He stressed that the pressing priority is to go all-out in search and rescue, relocate and look after those facing potential danger, provide urgent treatment to the injured, and minimize casualties. It is imperative to step up monitoring and early warning, ensure sound rescue operations and guard against secondary disasters. Premier Li Qiang also issued instructions, calling for swift verification of the number of missing persons and affected people and all-out rescue and relief efforts to ensure the prompt and orderly evacuation of people in danger. Vice Premier Zhang Guoqing has arrived at the site with officials from relevant departments to oversee the rescue and disaster-response operations. Relevant Chinese authorities have activated a national level-II emergency response for disaster relief. Xizang Autonomous Region has activated a level-I emergency response for natural disasters. Rescue forces from the military, armed police, border inspection, firefighting, and other relevant departments have rushed to the affected area at the earliest possible time, to join ongoing search and rescue operations. We are confident that under the strong leadership of the CPC Central Committee, people in the mudslide-hit area will overcome difficulties and rebuild their homes. The mudslide has caused massive casualties and left many missing in both China and Nepal. The Chinese side extends heartfelt sympathies to the government of Nepal and all those hit by the disaster. The two sides are having close communication and coordinating efforts for the search and rescue. The Chinese side is ready to provide emergency assistance in light of Nepal’s need. According to the information released so far by the local Chinese authorities, a total of 260 foreign nationals remain unaccounted for in the affected areas, with more specifics pending further verification due to the conditions on the ground. For Chinese rescuers, all lives are precious, regardless of their nationalities. We are communicating with relevant foreign embassies in China to keep them updated. As to the situation on the Nepalese side, nearly 100 Chinese nationals remain missing there. The Chinese Embassy in Nepal is seeking further verification with the Nepalese side and has put out a safety alert. Again we advise Chinese nationals there to move to safety and take precautions against secondary hazards. The Chinese Embassy in Nepal is available at all hours and will do its utmost to assist Chinese nationals in need. NHK: We have learned that a group of Japanese lawmakers visiting China met today with an official of the International Department of the CPC Central Committee. Could you provide more details about the meeting? Does the foreign ministry have any comment on it? Lin Jian: Chinese competent authorities will release information on the meeting in due course. The root cause of the serious difficulties in bilateral relations lies in the erroneous remarks and actions on Taiwan and in the fields of military and security made by those running the Japanese government. They should heed and value the voice of reason in Japan, do serious soul-searching, correct the wrongdoings, abide by the four political documents, and safeguard the political foundation of China-Japan relations with concrete actions. AFP: The U.S. law enforcement on Tuesday announced the seizure of Internet domains, allegedly used by Chinese hackers to target government agencies and critical infrastructure. The Justice Department and FBI said the seized domains were used by a Chinese state-sponsored hacking group, known as “QTFY” and by hacking platforms, known as “QScan” and “QTRouter.” I wonder if the foreign ministry can comment on this? Lin Jian: We notice relevant reports. China firmly opposes hacking and combats it in accordance with the law. China also firmly opposes spreading disinformation for political agenda. The so-called “statement” lacks evidence and confuses right and wrong. China strongly deplores and firmly opposes the U.S.’s wrong practice of slinging mud at China under the pretext of cybersecurity. The U.S. has been widely condemned as the world’s largest “hacking empire” and “eavesdropping empire,” with a blemished record and solid evidence to prove it. China has grave concerns with the U.S. on cybersecurity. The cases previously exposed, including the National Security Agency attacking and pre-positioning capability to disrupt China’s National Time Service Center, have laid bare the U.S. administration’s dangerous practice of carrying out cyberattacks on China’s critical infrastructure and pre-positioning cyberattack capabilities for potential large-scale destructive operations in the future. The U.S. side, however, has never made a response on this issue. When it comes to cyber issues, China and the U.S. are countries with big influence. The two sides should take the lead to safeguard and follow the international rules on cyberspace and jointly build a relationship in cyberspace featured by peace, stability and mutual respect. We urge the U.S. to quit double standards and political manipulation, take a responsible and constructive approach, and properly handle the risks on cybersecurity by equal-footed dialogue and consultation with China. Bloomberg: We’re wondering, with relation to the flash floods in Nepal and landslides in Tibet, could you give a breakdown of the nationalities of the foreign nationals? We’re also wondering if China is planning to take any special action to deal with the crisis? The second question is on Chinese leader’s planned trip to the U.S. We’re wondering if the Chinese leader will go to the U.S., and what conditions need to be met to ensure the trip is happening? Lin Jian: On your first question, affected by the disaster, the specific information is still under verification. The rescue efforts at the site are being carried out intensively and in an orderly manner. On your second question, China and the U.S. are in communication regarding interactions between the two heads of state this year. AFP: U.S. President Donald Trump declared a national emergency on Wednesday over foreign-made equipment inside the country’s electric grid, saying that the growing need for power has made the system a target for hostile governments. Can China provide a comment on this? Lin Jian: China consistently opposes overstretching the concept of national security to go after foreign enterprises. It is hoped that the U.S. will provide a fair, just and non-discriminatory business environment for companies of all countries. Reuters: About the mudslide in Gyirong County. We know that China is still verifying a lot of information about the foreigners, but is there any profile of the foreigners that we can have information about? Are they tourists? Are they workers who are working on projects along the border? Lin Jian: According to the initial information we have, there are tourists and pilgrims among those unaccounted for. For more specifics, as I just mentioned, we are waiting for further verification, which is still ongoing due to conditions on the ground.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Lin Jian’s Regular Press Conference on August 26, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
CCTV: China announced that President Xi Jinping will attend the 2026 SCO Summit. What message does China hope to convey? Lin Jian: This year marks the 25th anniversary of the founding of the SCO. Over the past 25 years, member states have upheld the Shanghai Spirit, worked in solidarity and coordination, and deepened all-round cooperation. The SCO has grown into a comprehensive regional cooperation organization that covers the biggest area and population with enormous development potential, successfully explored a new type of regional cooperation, and set an example of a new type of international relations. Last year’s SCO Summit in Tianjin provided strategic planning on the development of the SCO for the next decade, and opened up a new stage of high-quality development of the organization. At this year’s summit in Bishkek, President Xi Jinping will have in-depth exchanges of views with participating leaders on deepening SCO cooperation in various fields under the new circumstances and major international and regional issues of our times. They will provide guidance for the SCO’s high-quality development and participation in the reform and development of the global governance system. China stands ready to work with various parties to build up consensus and write a new chapter of cooperation in Bishkek, and contribute to security, stability, development and revitalization of regional countries and the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. CGTN: President Xi Jinping will pay a state visit to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt. Could you share with us the arrangement? What’s China’s expectation on growing its ties with the two countries? Lin Jian: China and Kyrgyzstan are good neighbors connected by mountains and rivers, good friends of mutual trust, and good partners with a common pursuit. Since the establishment of diplomatic relations 34 years ago, the two countries have been treating each other with good faith and sincerity, setting a stellar example of mutual support and mutual success among neighboring countries. In recent years, China-Kyrgyzstan relations have grown by leaps and bounds, with consolidating political mutual trust, fruitful outcomes in high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, numerous highlights of people-to-people exchanges, and close and effective coordination on international occasions. Last year, President Xi Jinping had three meetings with President Japarov, steering China-Kyrgyzstan cooperation into a golden period of rapid development. During the visit, President Xi Jinping will have an in-depth exchange of views on bilateral relations, cooperation in key areas, and international and regional situation with President Japarov in their talks, and attend various state events. China looks forward to working with Kyrgyzstan to take this visit as an opportunity to promote high-quality development of mutually beneficial cooperation on all fronts, add new dimensions to the China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future, and bring more benefits to the two peoples. Egypt is the first Arab and African country to establish diplomatic relations with New China. In recent years, under the strategic guidance of President Xi Jinping and President El-Sisi, the two countries have deepened political mutual trust, achieved fruitful outcomes in cooperation across various fields, and engaged in increasingly frequent people-to-people exchanges and close and effective coordination on multilateral occasions. China-Egypt comprehensive strategic partnership has grown by leaps and bounds, and been at its best in history, setting a stellar example of solidarity, collaboration and mutual benefit among developing countries. This visit marks President Xi Jinping’s first state visit to Egypt in 10 years. As we are celebrating the 70th anniversary of the establishment of China-Egypt diplomatic relations, this visit carries great significance in building on the past achievements and charting the future. During the visit, President Xi Jinping will hold talks with President El-Sisi. They will have an in-depth exchange of views on China-Egypt relations and international and regional issues of mutual interest. Through the visit, China looks forward to working with Egypt to carry forward traditional friendship, render each other firm support, expand mutually beneficial cooperation, and bolster each other’s modernization, so that we can jointly draw a new chapter of China-Egypt relations and make positive contributions to peace and stability in the region and beyond. Bloomberg: Following Scott Bessent’s public comments on the so-called “Economic D-Day” regarding sanctions on Iran and its trading partners, has there been any communication between the U.S. and the Chinese side on this matter? And if so, can you provide any additional details? Lin Jian: I have no information to share at the moment. Bloomberg: Chinese authorities are urging Chinese citizens in Eswatini to evacuate, and urging others not to visit the country, citing local security and scamming concerns. Can you elaborate a little bit on some of the thinking behind this advisory? Could you also tell me how many Chinese citizens roughly live in Eswatini? Lin Jian: Eswatini is faced with a complex security situation with rampant telecom fraud and online gambling and extremely high safety risks. Issuing travel advisories is a common practice worldwide. Committed to a people-centered approach and diplomacy for the people, we will do everything necessary to safeguard the safety and legitimate rights and interests of Chinese citizens overseas. Bloomberg: Would you be able to give me some examples of other similar travel advisories that China has issued, specifically regarding scamming and related risks? And also, China doesn’t have diplomatic relations with Eswatini. Is that a factor in this advisory or is it unrelated? Lin Jian: We have issued similar advisories. For this one, I need to stress that given the extremely high safety risks and rampant telecom fraud and online gambling in Eswatini, the Chinese government, for the safety of Chinese nationals, issued the travel advisory after prudent evaluation. Bloomberg: Going back a little bit to the SCO and also the trips to Egypt by President Xi Jinping. You mentioned that international and regional issues would be on the agendas in both Kyrgyzstan and Egypt. Specifically, can I ask you, how prominent do you think Iran will feature in the discussions? Is there anything a bit more specific you could share about what regional conflicts in particular will be dealt with as part of this trip? Lin Jian: For more about the visits, we will release readouts in due course. Please stay tuned. Bloomberg: We know that Canada has matched the tariffs that President Trump set, including 50 percent on items such as dairy and steel. Broadly speaking, is there some kind of opinion or perspective that you could share from the Chinese foreign ministry’s point of view in terms of the actions that Canada or perhaps other countries might take in response to Trump’s tariff war. Is there some advice, for example, or some comments that you can provide? Lin Jian: China believes that economic and trade concerns should be addressed through dialogue and consultation on an equal footing.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Lin Jian’s Regular Press Conference on August 25, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-25
Beijing Daily: Last week, Beijing hosted the 2026 World Robot Conference and the second World Humanoid Robot Games opened at the National Speed Skating Oval (the “Ice Ribbon”). Chinese humanoid robots broke multiple human records, including the 100-meter sprint and the men’s high jump, which sparked heated discussion worldwide. Meanwhile, some commentators suggest that the outlook for the industrial deployment and commercialization is uncertain. They also contend that China faces headwinds in sharing opportunities with the world, given the preventive and restrictive measures imposed by certain countries on its high-tech industries. What’s your comment? Lin Jian: There has been extensive coverage of these events. Beyond the sporting events, what is more noteworthy is that humanoid robots are rapidly moving out of labs into real-world industries. They sort packages and assemble parts on factory floors, assist with elderly care and early childhood education in communities, and play ping-pong or fold clothes with dexterity. Behind these advances are OEMs, core part makers and algorithm developers working in concert, backed by China’s consistent policy support, robust innovation capabilities and diverse application scenarios. At its core, China’s pursuit of new quality productive forces and technological innovation is about open cooperation and mutual benefit, not about setting up restrictions or seeking exclusive control. China stands ready to work with all other countries to continue dialogue and cooperation on artificial intelligence, embodied intelligence and other frontier areas, so that “innovation in China” and “intelligent manufacturing in China” can translate into a driving force for shared development, cooperation potential can be unlocked through technological connectivity, joint standard-setting and shared markets, and innovation dividends can be better delivered to humanity. AFP: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday laid out plans for the economic asphyxiation of Iran, expanding Washington’s secondary sanction threats and warning of dire consequences for countries that do not join the campaign. I wonder if China has a comment on this? (Similar question from CNBC) Lin Jian: China has made clear on many occasions its firm opposition to illicit unilateral sanctions that have no basis in international law or the authorization of the UN Security Council. Economic warfare and maximum pressure provide no solution. On the contrary, they only serve to fuel tensions and lead to risk spillover, which will disrupt the global economic and financial order, and harm the legitimate rights and interests of other countries. The pressing task is to facilitate the deescalation of the situation and return to dialogue and negotiation as soon as possible. China will do everything necessary to firmly safeguard its rights and interests. AFP: U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration on Monday moved to impose a fee of more than US$100,000 on employers hiring foreign workers through the highly skilled H-1B visa program. And given that around 12 percent of H-1B holders in 2025 were from China, do you have a comment on this? Lin Jian: I have no comment on the U.S. visa policy. Bloomberg: Following on the developments with the U.S. sanctions relating to Iran, we saw that there have been new sanctions on entities, individuals and vessels, including on some Chinese firms. Is China willing to change some of its behaviors and interactions with Iran to comply with U.S. demands? If so, what kind of actions is China considering to take? Lin Jian: China’s cooperation with Iran is conducted within the framework of international law, thus should not be disrupted. China is closely following the developments, and will do everything necessary to firmly safeguard its rights and interests. CNBC: The U.S. said that it would give countries a timeline on when to shut down the actions that it has identified. We’re wondering if China has received any sort of timeline or has any plans to address the China-based entities and individuals named in the Treasury announcement? Lin Jian: We are closely following the developments, and will do everything necessary to firmly safeguard our rights and interests.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Lin Jian’s Regular Press Conference on August 24, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-24
As agreed between the two sides, Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, Director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs, and China’s Special Representative on the Boundary Question Between China and India Wang Yi will co-chair the 25th Round of Talks Between the Special Representatives on the Boundary Question with India’s Special Representative and National Security Advisor Ajit Doval in Beijing on August 25. CCTV: Foreign Minister Wang Yi has just concluded a successful visit to Indonesia, where the first Conference of the China-Indonesia Comprehensive Strategic Dialogue Mechanism and the Second Ministerial Meeting of the China-Indonesia Joint Foreign and Defense Dialogue were held. Could you give more details about the two meetings? Lin Jian: The Comprehensive Strategic Dialogue Mechanism is a new mechanism established between China and Indonesia. It provides vital institutional support for deepening bilateral cooperation across the “five pillars” under new circumstances. Foreign Minister Wang Yi and his Indonesian counterpart held a successful first conference. They spoke highly of the progress in cooperation across various fields, and agreed to deepen the alignment of development strategies and launch the formulation of a new five-year action plan for bilateral ties. The two sides agreed to set more ambitious bilateral trade targets and vigorously expand cooperation in new-quality productive forces such as artificial intelligence. The two sides reached an agreement to restart cooperation in fishing, accelerate maritime cooperation and push forward joint development. Both sides agreed that deepening cooperation in energy and mineral resources serves their common interests, and expressed readiness to jointly build a comprehensive, open and green partnership in this area. China stands ready to better assist Indonesia in transforming its resource advantages into momentum for development, accelerating the country’s industrialization process and benefiting the Indonesian people. Indonesia spoke highly of the contributions made by Chinese companies in Indonesia to local development, noting that the success of Chinese companies is also a success for Indonesia. It expressed readiness to provide Chinese companies with a fair, transparent and friendly business environment. The China-Indonesia Joint Foreign and Defense Dialogue is the first ministerial-level “2+2” mechanism China has established globally, and this marks the second meeting of the mechanism. The two sides agreed on the need to coordinate the two major tasks of development and security, foster a sense of security partnership, support each other’s core interests, jointly oppose external interference, and strive for greater progress in political security and defense cooperation. Both will safeguard the overall momentum of regional cooperation and maintain peace and stability in the South China Sea, strengthen policy coordination on multilateral platforms, oppose unilateral bullying and power politics, and safeguard international fairness, justice and the legitimate rights and interests of developing countries. The world is currently at a crossroads between unity and division, and between cooperation and confrontation. As major developing countries and key members of the Global South, China and Indonesia’s efforts to strengthen strategic coordination and deepen solidarity and cooperation bear great significance far beyond the bilateral dimension. The success of China-Indonesia cooperation is also a success for the Global South. Guided by the strategic common understandings reached by the two heads of state, China stands ready to work with Indonesia to effectively translate consensus from the mechanism meetings into outcomes, expand and deepen all-round strategic cooperation, address risks and challenges, bolster respective modernization, and contribute more to stability and prosperity in the region and beyond. China-Arab TV: King Abdullah II of Jordan is visiting China. We notice that an increasing number of leaders of Arab nations have visited China. China’s influence is on the rise, and China is playing an increasingly important role in the Arab world. What are the outcomes of King Abdullah II’s visit to China? What’s China’s expectation for China-Arab cooperation in the next couple of years? Lin Jian: China and Jordan enjoy traditional friendship. Under the strategic guidance of President Xi Jinping and King Abdullah II, China-Jordan relations have sustained the momentum of growth, bringing tangible benefits to the two peoples. China will work with Jordan to take the visit as an opportunity to help China-Jordan strategic partnership produce more fruits, and open up new prospects and inject new impetus into growing the bilateral ties. We will release more information on this visit in due course. You are welcome to stay tuned. In recent years, China-Arab relations enjoy robust development, setting a stellar example of solidarity and cooperation between developing countries. China will work with Arab countries to carry forward traditional friendship, deepen strategic mutual trust, promote mutually beneficial cooperation, and foster closer people-to-people exchanges so as to bring China-Arab relations and cooperation to a new height. AFP: Sources told AFP and other media outlets that China is weighing a bid to host UN climate talks in 2028. I wonder if you can confirm this or comment on this? Lin Jian: We do not have information on that for the time being. The Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change is an important platform for global climate governance. China will continue its active support for and participation in it. Beijing Daily: Does China have any comment on the Kurultai elections Kazakhstan held yesterday? Lin Jian: China congratulates Kazakhstan on holding smooth Kurultai elections yesterday. As a friendly neighbor and permanent comprehensive strategic partner, China supports Kazakhstan in independently following a development path befitting its national conditions, and is glad to see sustained security and economic prosperity in the country. We wish Kazakhstan new and greater achievements in national development. China values its relations with Kazakhstan and stands ready to work with Kazakhstan to deliver on the important common understandings between the two presidents, deepen all-round mutually beneficial cooperation, and bring the bilateral relations to a new height. Yonhap News Agency: Today marks the 34th anniversary of ROK-China diplomatic ties. How does China see the significance of this relationship and what are its expectations for bilateral ties going forward? Lin Jian: Indeed, today marks the 34th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and the ROK. Over the past 34 years, our two countries, as friendly neighbors, have become inseparable strategic cooperative partners with all‑round and rapid growth in political cooperation, economy and trade, people‑to‑people and cultural exchanges. Facts have proven that the development of bilateral relations is in keeping with the trend of the times, serves the shared interests of both countries, and contributes to regional peace and development. At present, China-ROK relations continue to improve and develop along the direction charted by the two heads of state. Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Foreign Minister Wang Yi just paid a visit to the ROK upon invitation, where he had in-depth exchanges with the ROK side on advancing the sound and sustainable development of bilateral ties. China has always placed the ROK high on its agenda for neighborhood diplomacy and stands ready to work with the ROK side to implement the common understandings reached by the two heads of state, bring bilateral strategic cooperative partnership to new heights, and deliver more benefits to the two peoples. PTI: You just announced the special representative talks between India and China tomorrow. It is a unique, indeed, a very comprehensive mechanism to discuss the overall relations. Maybe you can highlight what are the issues that could be discussed in tomorrow’s talks? Lin Jian: The Talks Between the Special Representatives of China and India on the Boundary Question are the main channel for negotiations between China and India on the boundary question, and also an important platform for communication on issues of mutual interest. In August last year, China and India successfully held the 24th round of talks, during which the two sides had candid and in-depth exchanges of views on the boundary question and reached a number of common understandings. During this round of talks, the two sides will continue the in-depth communication on the boundary question in the spirit of the common understandings between leaders of the two countries to jointly keep the border areas peaceful and tranquil. The two sides will also exchange views on bilateral relations and international and regional issues. China News Service: We notice that following the UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres’s attendance at the 2026 World AI Conference & High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance in China, UN Deputy Secretary-General attended a dialogue on AI and human development in Xi’an. Can you share more details? Lin Jian: From August 20 to 21, a dialogue on Artificial Intelligence and Human Development was held in Xi’an. The event was co-hosted by China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the UN. UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina J. Mohammed attended and addressed the event. The outcomes of the dialogue will be submitted to the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly. Not long ago, taking a broader view of social progress, President Xi Jinping shared four observations on the opportunities and challenges brought by AI, stressing the need to adhere to the principle of openness and win-win, strengthen risk-awareness, encourage inclusiveness, and advocate solidarity, which are well-received by the international community. The purpose of this event echoes the important statements of President Xi. Representatives from various countries have explored the profound impact of AI on human development through the lenses of history, philosophy and reality. The attendance of UN Secretary-General and Deputy Secretary-General at international conferences on AI in China fully demonstrates the significance of AI, a cutting-edge technology, for the world, and also reflects that China always supports the UN’s role as the main channel in global AI governance. Xi’an is where the ancient Silk Road begins and where the East meets the West, and embodies the history of mutual learning and harmonious coexistence among civilizations. Such a place can help various parties draw wisdom from the long history, answer the questions of the times brought by AI, and promote the common welfare of all countries. Participants from various countries noted that in developing AI, it’s important to take a people-centered approach, develop AI for the positive and for good, share the opportunities, and shoulder the responsibilities together. More emphasis should be put on the interests of developing countries and the disadvantaged groups, and AI can be used to empower human development and progress of civilizations. China will, together with the UN and all countries in the world, make continuous efforts to ensure the open and inclusive development of AI for good and for all so as to better contribute to the common welfare of the international community. Reuters: The U.S. Treasury Secretary has threatened secondary sanctions against countries that trade or deal with Iran. China has historically been a major buyer of Iranian oil. If the U.S. does impose secondary sanctions tomorrow, what will be the response from China? (Similar question from Bloomberg) Lin Jian: Sanctions and pressure tactics do no help in resolving issues. They will only lead to escalation that serves no one’s interest. China calls on parties to act rationally and with restraint, and avoid taking any measure that may further escalate tensions or deal another blow to global economic growth and financial stability. They need to return to the right track of political settlement through dialogue and negotiation at an early date. China will closely watch relevant developments and do what is necessary to protect our legitimate rights and interests. Global Times: A U.S. official in a recent social media post alleged that high‑risk technologies from Chinese tech companies create risks of espionage, cyber‑attacks, and network disruptions, urging U.S. partners across the Western hemisphere to rapidly shift to reliable supply vendors to protect their citizens and sovereignty. Would you like to comment on this? Lin Jian: The allegations, full of fact-distorting fabrications, are means of blatant tech‑bullying and unilateral coercion. China firmly rejects them. Chinese tech firms have become well-known for their advanced technologies, competitive pricing and secure and efficient services. When operating overseas, they strictly abide by local laws, regulations and industry norms. In fact, they have won wide recognition and appreciation from local partners and communities, contributed to host‑country socioeconomic growth and job creation, and proven themselves genuinely reliable suppliers. In stark contrast, the U.S. has long engaged in tapping, surveillance, and cyber-attacks across Latin America and the Caribbean, leaving nations there feeling insecure and distrustful of Washington. We advise the U.S. to stop its political manipulation, stop interfering with sovereign nations’ right to independently choose cooperation partners, and instead contribute to prosperity and stability in Latin America and the Caribbean through concrete actions. Beijing Youth Daily: Concerning the case that Hong Kong’s High Court convicted the “Hong Kong Alliance” and its former leaders Lee Cheuk-yan, Ho Chun-yan and Chow Hang-tung of inciting subversion, the EU and certain countries including the U.S. have expressed their concerns in their statements and remarks. What’s China’s response? Lin Jian: Certain countries and institutions used the judicial case to make malicious smears against Hong Kong and its rule of law, and interfered in China’s internal affair. China firmly opposes it and has lodged serious protests. The platform of “Hong Kong Alliance” is aimed at subverting state power at its core. The facts concerning the defendants’ crimes are clear and the offense has caused serious harm. It’s legitimate and lawful for the government of Hong Kong SAR to combat the activities endangering national security. Hong Kong upholds rule of law. The central government firmly supports the Hong Kong SAR in safeguarding national security and combating activities that endanger national security in accordance with the law. Hong Kong affairs are purely China’s internal affairs. We urge relevant parties to earnestly respect China’s sovereignty and the rule of law in Hong Kong, and stop the political manipulation and interference in the Hong Kong affairs and China’s internal affairs in any form. Bloomberg: I would like to ask about the meeting that Vice Foreign Minister Miao Deyu had with Iran’s Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi in Beijing. Does the ministry have any more details on that meeting? Lin Jian: China has shared details about the meeting in a readout, which you may refer to. I have nothing to add. China is closely following the situation in the Middle East and Gulf region and has been actively committed to promoting talks for peace. We stand ready to act in the spirit of the four propositions put forward by President Xi Jinping on safeguarding and promoting peace and stability in the Middle East and make continued effort to help restore peace and tranquility to the Middle East at an early date. Antara: Another question about the China-Indonesia Comprehensive Strategic Dialogue Mechanism. In the past, Indonesia and China had the High-Level Dialogue Cooperation Mechanism, which led to flagship projects such as the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway. Now China and Indonesia held the China-Indonesia Comprehensive Strategic Dialogue Mechanism. Are there any joint projects similar to the high-speed railway that are expected to become the result from this newly established dialogue mechanism? Lin Jian: The China‑Indonesia Comprehensive Strategic Dialogue is an important joint measure implementing the consensus between the two heads of state. It aims to deepen practical cooperation across the fields, advance the building of a community with a shared future, and deliver tangible benefits to both peoples. The Jakarta‑Bandung High‑Speed Railway has served over 16 million passengers with safe and smooth operation since its opening. It has improved local transport conditions and made travel easier for residents along the route, and continues to provide momentum for Indonesia’s economic and social development and regional connectivity. China stands ready to work with Indonesia to make full use of the Comprehensive Strategic Dialogue mechanism, advance high‑quality Belt and Road cooperation, produce more cooperation outcomes in infrastructure and other fields, and inject fresh impetus into our respective modernization.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Lin Jian’s Regular Press Conference on August 21, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-21
At the invitation of Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Kuwait Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah will pay an official visit to China from August 23 to 24. Shenzhen TV: On August 20, in the Bangladeshi presidential election, Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir from the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party was declared the winner and became the 23rd president of Bangladesh. What’s your comment? What’s China’s expectation on China-Bangladesh relations in the years to come? Lin Jian: China congratulates Mr. Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on his election as the president of Bangladesh. China values its relations with Bangladesh, and stands ready to work with the Bangladeshi government to deliver on the important common understandings between the leaders, promote high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, expand exchanges and cooperation in various areas, and strive for new progress in building the China-Bangladesh community with a shared future in the new era. Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting: Donald Trump has threatened to wage a full-fledged economic war on Iran. Many say the economic threat is aimed at making up for the failure of the war, in the military domain, that the U.S. and Israel waged against Iran. What’s your take on that? Lin Jian: Sanctions and pressure tactics are not the solution. China calls on parties to act responsibly and stick to the political and diplomatic approach. Phoenix TV: A cross-party group of Japanese lawmakers will reportedly visit China next week, noting that the status quo of Japan-China relations is in no one’s interest. They hope to play a role in improving the bilateral ties. What’s your comment? Lin Jian: We notice that some visionary people from both Japan’s ruling and opposition parties are deeply concerned over the current state of China-Japan relations and wish to make an effort to restore the relations to the right track. We call on those running the government of Japan to take these concerns seriously, abide by the four political documents, and create the conditions necessary for normal exchanges between China and Japan with concrete actions. Yonhap News Agency: Yesterday the DPRK fired over ten ballistic missiles toward waters to its east. This marks its 12th launch this year and the largest-scale launch in three years. Does China have any comment? Lin Jian: We noted the reports and do not have any new comment. Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting: Iran has endured years of sanctions imposed by the U.S. The Islamic Republic has either managed to bypass or find alternatives. And now it is said that Trump has no tangible card to enforce what he claims as “toughest sanctions.” What’s your viewpoint? Lin Jian: China believes that military means, sanctions and pressure tactics are not the solution. On the contrary, they will only lead to escalation that serves no one’s interests. We call for efforts to solve disputes through dialogue and negotiation. AFP: A follow-up on Iran, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged China to join Washington in putting strong economic pressure on Iran. This was in an interview yesterday. Bessent noted that China has historically imported much of its energy from the Gulf. Does the foreign ministry have a response to these comments by Bessent? Lin Jian: I answered a similar question yesterday. Let me reiterate, China opposes illicit unilateral sanctions that lack basis in international law and UN Security Council mandate. We call on parties to act responsibly and stick to the political and diplomatic approach.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Lin Jian’s Regular Press Conference on August 20, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-20
China Daily: We notice that recent articles by economists including Dani Rodrik, professor at Harvard Kennedy School, and Michael R. Strain, director of economic policy studies at the American Enterprise Institute, have refuted the so-called “China shock” and “China squeeze” narratives. They believe that China’s trade policy is not “beggar-thy-neighbor” but rather “enriches-thy-neighbor”; beyond finished goods, China is also a major exporter of production machinery, components and intermediate goods, helping reduce the cost of industrialization for many countries; asking China to voluntarily give way to other countries at the expense of its domestic industry is an off-base economic narrative. What’s your comment on this? Lin Jian: We noted that more and more people with insights in the world have expressed similar views. Facts have proven that China brings the world not “shocks” but opportunities; it does not “squeeze” but enables growth. The affordable quality products made in China has lowered the threshold of industrialization for developing countries. China’s open-source and universally beneficial innovation has enabled more countries to access affordable cutting-edge technologies. China’s stable and reliable supply has strengthened the resilience of the global industrial and supply chains, and supported Global South countries’ pursuit of modernization at a faster pace. In the face of growing uncertainties and instabilities in the world economy, China will continue to offer more dividends of its market, innovation and development to other countries through high-quality development. Bloomberg: U.S. President Donald Trump has announced plans to inflict what he calls an “economic D-Day” against Iran, including threats to Iran’s trading partners. Given that China buys a large amount of Iran’s oil, for example, does the foreign ministry have comment on this economic warfare approach that Trump is threatening and how it might impact China? Even though China hasn’t been directly mentioned, I think the implication is a safe one to draw. What’s the foreign ministry’s comment on President Trump’s economic warfare? Lin Jian: Sanctions and pressure tactics are not the solution. China calls on parties to act responsibly and stick to the political and diplomatic approach. AFP: U.S. President Donald Trump said yesterday that he will meet North Korean leader later this year. According to a report by the Wall Street Journal, he is considering having that meeting at the APEC summit in November. I’d like to ask as the potential host of this meeting and as a country that has close ties, what is China’s comment on this? Lin Jian: On the meeting between the DPRK and the U.S. you just mentioned, I don’t have any specific information. I will not comment on this. Bloomberg: Regarding the meetings between Foreign Minister Wang Yi and his South Korean counterpart in South Korea. The Korean side is saying that Foreign Minister Wang Yi had said that China is actively considering a meeting between President Xi and President Lee on the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen. I was wondering if you could confirm this meeting plan? If so, can you offer some more details on that? Lin Jian: As the host country of this year’s APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting, China stands ready to take this opportunity to work with all sides, including the ROK, to build an Asia-Pacific community and inject new impetus for peace and development in the Asia Pacific and beyond. As to the specifics you mentioned, we will release information in due course.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson’s Remarks on Japanese Politicians Paying Respects to the Yasukuni War Shrine Which Honors Class-A War Criminals
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-15
Q: August 15 marks the day of Japan’s unconditional surrender in the Second World War. Prime Minister of Japan Sanae Takaichi made a monetary offering to the Yasukuni war shrine today, and certain cabinet members also visited the shrine. What’s your comment? A: China strongly deplores Japan’s negative moves related to the Yasukuni war shrine, and has lodged serious protests against Japan. During WWII, Japan launched the war of aggression and committed horrendous crimes. The Yasukuni war shrine is a spiritual tool and symbol of Japanese militarism. It is in fact a shrine for war criminals, as it honors 14 convicted Class-A war criminals responsible for the war of aggression. No pretext whatsoever can hide the Japanese politicians’ true intention which is to change the verdict on the war criminals, cover up Japan’s war crimes, distort the historical facts, and pave the way for accelerating remilitarization. This is an affront to historical justice, a challenge to the foundational norms of civilization, and a provocation against the postwar international order. Such behaviors have been firmly rejected by the overwhelming majority of the international community. This year marks the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trials. To view and treat history correctly is an important prerequisite for Japan’s postwar return to the international community, the political foundation for Japan’s ties with neighboring countries, and more importantly, a key measure for Japan’s commitment to peaceful development. We urge the Japanese side to do serious soul-searching on its history of aggression, make a clean break with militarism, and earn trust from its Asian neighbors and the rest of the world with concrete actions.
